Hi Ava,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is the formal RFP we circulated internally (MSH_RFP_2026.pdf). We're evaluating vendors for a private inference deployment in our clinical analytics environment. Primary concerns are: air-gapped installability, operator access controls, patch and SBOM process, and evidence for KMS/HSM integrations.

We've included an "Operational Scenarios" appendix that outlines three run states we need validated (normal ops, emergency patching with no outbound internet, and DR failover between two on-prem sites). Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide written responses for the scenarios and a short operator runbook sample?

Target: receive your responses and any artifacts within five business days (by 2026-09-24). Also please note any required involvement from our infra/security teams.

Ava / team — quick clarifications following our infra review: 

- Primary images: RHEL 8.6 (preferred) and Ubuntu 22.04 as fallback.
- We will be using on-prem HSM appliances (Thales Luna) for key storage; FIPS compliance is required for crypto operations.
- Network: internal-only DNS, strictly no outbound internet from the cluster except through an approved jump host during scheduled maintenance windows.
- Patching model: we require a documented maintenance window process that supports applying signed kernel and runtime patches when the cluster is offline for up to 48 hours.

Also, the Operational Scenarios sheet includes a table we expect you to fill: operator actions, preconditions, expected logs/artifacts, escalation path. Can you populate that and include sample log entries to demonstrate auditability?

I'll attach the appendix export for reference.

Thanks,
Liam

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-23 16:45 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP: Offline / VPC Deployment Capabilities for MediSys — responses and artifacts (see attachments)

Liam — thank you for the clarifications. Please find our delivered artifacts attached and inline answers to the Operational Scenarios table below. We've structured the packet so your security and infra reviewers can jump to each section.

Attachments included: REDWOOD_PrivateDeploy_Answers_20260923.pdf, redwood_operator_runbook_sample.md, REDWOOD_SBOM_and_patching_overview.pdf

Inline highlights (abridged):

1) Supported OS and install model
  - RHEL 8.6: certified install image and kickstart configuration available.
  - Ubuntu 22.04: supported as a fallback; package manifest differs.
  - Install modes: automated airgap installer (ISO + artifact bundle), and an orchestration-driven bundle for bare-metal + K8s on-prem.

2) HSM / KMS integration
  - We integrate with Thales Luna (plug-in + PKCS#11) and common cloud KMS.
  - Key usage model: customer-managed keys only; private deploy control plane does not hold key material.
  - We provide an HSM proof-of-concept run demonstrating sign/unwrap operations; logs include HSM tx IDs for audit correlation.

3) Network / egress constraints
  - Installer supports fully air-gapped installs. Maintenance/pull-through options use an approved jump host with signed manifests; all outbound connections are optional and auditable.

4) Patching and SBOM
  - We produce an SBOM (CycloneDX format) per release and a signed patch manifest.
  - Offline patch process: operator stages signed artifacts locally, runs a validation step (hash + signature), and applies updates via our orchestration tool.
  - Expected downtime and rollback procedures are documented in the attached runbook sample.

5) Operator model and audit trails
  - Least-privilege operator accounts (RBAC) with session recordings and an approval workflow for emergency actions.
  - Audit artifacts: operator session logs, API request traces, package install receipts, and HSM transaction IDs.

6) Operational scenarios (filled table — abridged):
  - Normal ops: operator runs daily health check; automated KV cache warm-up; expected logs: /var/log/redwood/serve.log entries and per-request token-latency traces.
  - Emergency offline patching: precondition = patch bundle present on internal share; operator steps = validate signatures -> quiesce feeds -> apply -> smoke test; expected artifacts = patch-manifest.sig, migration.log, and per-node health checks.
  - DR failover: replication via snapshot + manual promotion; operator action = promote-secondary -> update DNS -> validate service; expected artifacts = snapshot-checksum.txt and replication-audit.log.

Artifacts we attached include sample log excerpts and template entries for each expected artifact named above.

Next steps / asks from MediSys:
- Confirm whether you want the runbook to reference your specific Thales model (we can embed model-specific commands if you provide access to a test appliance).
- Would your security team like a short remote workshop (1.5h) to walk through the runbook and KMS integration? We can schedule next week.

If this looks good I can convert the PDF into a signed delivery (DocuSign) and add a short SOW for an on-site install engagement.

Regards,
Ava Chen
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
